help.title: Rules reference
help.lead: Tap a topic to read it. In the game, tap an icon on an enlarged card: a short explanation appears with a "More" button.
help.round.title: The round
help.round.short: Each round everyone secretly picks 2 cards, the cards are revealed, everyone acts by initiative, then you may rest.
help.round.body:
The game is played in rounds, and every round has four steps. Chance comes from the initiative die, the attack modifier deck and the monsters' behaviour cards.

{icon:hand} **Choose cards.** Each player secretly picks 2 cards from their hand and marks one as leading. Or declares a long rest.

{icon:initiative} **Reveal.** Everyone's cards are revealed at once, a behaviour card is revealed for each monster type, and everyone rolls the initiative die.

{icon:hero} **Turns.** Heroes and monsters act one after another by initiative: the lower number goes first.

{icon:rest} **End of round.** Orbs and elements weaken, "until end of round" bonuses end, and heroes with at least 2 cards in their discard are offered a short rest.
help.cards.title: Two cards and the leading one
help.cards.short: Each round you pick 2 cards; the leading one gives its initiative number.
help.cards.body:
Your ability cards are both your actions and your "stamina" for the scenario. Each round pick **two** cards from your hand. Tap a card to pick it; a long press shows it large.

Mark one of the two as **leading** {icon:initiative}. The number in its circle is your initiative this round: the lower the number, the earlier you act.

Strong cards often have a high number (you act late), defensive ones a low number (you act early). Choose the leading card by when you need to act: strike before the monster, or wait for it to come closer first.

Cards do not return to your hand on their own: played cards go to the discard, so sooner or later you will have to rest.
help.halves.title: Top and bottom of a card
help.halves.short: On your turn play the top action of one card and the bottom action of the other, in any order.
help.halves.body:
Every card has a **top** and a **bottom** half. The top usually attacks or defends, the bottom usually moves.

On your turn you play the **top of one** card and the **bottom of the other**. You choose the order: you may move first and strike afterwards.

Instead of what is written on a half you may play the **basic action**: top — {icon:attack} Attack 2, bottom — {icon:move} Move 2. The card still goes to the discard.

You may skip part of an action (for example, not move), but you cannot reorder its parts.
help.initiative.title: Initiative
help.initiative.short: The number on the leading card plus a die: lower acts earlier.
help.initiative.body:
Initiative is a number from 1 to 99 that sets the order of turns in a round. A hero's comes from the leading card, a monster's from its behaviour card.

**Initiative die.** Once the cards are revealed, every hero and every monster type adds a d12 to the number on the card. The game does the sum and shows it: "25 + 7 = 32". Close cards sometimes swap places, distant ones never. The die can be turned off in Settings → "Rules".

The initiative bar at the top shows the round's order from left to right. Whoever has acted fades, and whoever is acting is shown larger.

If a hero and a monster have the same number, the hero goes first. Monsters of one type act together: elites first, then normal ones.

A long rest has initiative 99 and does not roll: you act last.

While choosing cards, agree with intent tokens: "attacking", "healing", "approaching", "going early" or "going late". Everyone sees them, but not the cards.
help.turn.title: A hero's turn
help.turn.short: Pick a card half, then a hex or a target on the board, confirm; do it twice and end the turn.
help.turn.body:
When your turn comes, your two chosen cards are shown at the bottom.

1. Tap the half of a card you want to play.
2. The board lights up where you can go or whom you can hit. Tap a hex or an enemy, then tap again (or the confirm button).
3. Play a half of the other card.
4. Press "End turn".

At the end of the turn you pick up coins on your hex, and the played cards go to the discard, the lost pile or the active area.
help.undo.title: Undo
help.undo.short: As long as nothing random has happened, a step can be undone.
help.undo.body:
The {icon:undo} "Undo" button takes you back to the start of the card half you are playing.

You can undo until an attack modifier is drawn or a new room is opened: whatever already depends on chance stays.
help.goals.title: Scenario goal
help.goals.short: Every scenario has its own goal; you lose when no hero is left standing or a goal condition fails.
help.goals.body:
The scenario goal is written in the introduction and in the goal line at the top: defeat all monsters or the boss, reach the exit, bring an item, survive, defend a zone, escape, escort, collect or destroy.

The scenario is lost if all heroes are exhausted (in the Fork: downed or exhausted). Some goals have their own way to lose too: a monster in the defence zone, a downed companion, time running out.

For a victory each hero gets bonus experience and gold; coins collected on the board turn into gold too. Secondary goals give more.
help.hints.title: Hints
help.hints.short: Three hint levels, for each hero separately, in the settings.
help.hints.body:
Hints are switched on for each hero separately, so one can play with hints and another without.

**Level 1 — Explanations.** When a rule appears for the first time (a condition, an orb, a trap), a short explanation pops up with a "More" button.

**Level 2 — Monster intents.** After the cards are revealed, arrows show whom each monster is going to attack.

**Level 3 — Advice.** A "What to do?" button suggests a useful move (coming later).

Change the level in "Settings" or before the game on the new game screen.
help.tutorial.title: Tutorial
help.tutorial.short: A short scenario with step-by-step hints.
help.tutorial.body:
The tutorial is a small scenario with one Warden and a few rats. A helper shows where to tap and explains why.

You can stop it at any time and play it again from the main menu with the "Tutorial" button. The rules there are the usual ones, only the deck is shuffled so that the first turns go well.
help.move.title: Movement
help.move.short: Move N: walk up to N hexes; obstacles, enemies and walls are in the way.
help.move.body:
{icon:move} **Move N** lets you walk up to N hexes. The board lights up every hex you can reach; tap the one you want and confirm.

You may pass through allies but not stop on their hex. You cannot pass through enemies, obstacles or walls.

**Difficult terrain** costs 2 movement per hex. A **trap** springs when you step on it and disappears. **Hazardous terrain** deals damage on every step.

An immobilized hero cannot move at all.
help.terrain.title: Terrain and traps
help.terrain.short: Obstacles cannot be crossed, difficult terrain costs 2 movement, a trap hits once and is gone.
help.terrain.body:
**Obstacles** (barrels, rocks, pillars) cannot be walked through, but sometimes you can see through them.

**Difficult terrain** (bushes, rubble) costs 2 movement per hex.

{icon:trap} A **trap** springs as soon as a figure steps on it: 2 + scenario level damage, sometimes a condition too. Then the trap disappears. Monsters walk around traps if there is another way.

**Hazardous terrain** deals damage on every step through it.

**Walls** block both movement and line of sight.
help.jump.title: Jump and flying
help.jump.short: A jump ignores everything on the way except the landing spot; flying ignores terrain and figures.
help.jump.body:
{icon:jump} **Jump**: the move ignores everything on the way (figures, obstacles, traps); only the landing spot matters.

{icon:fly} **Flying**: the figure flies over terrain and figures, and traps below it do not spring.
help.doors.title: Doors and breakable obstacles
help.doors.short: Step on a door to open it: a room with monsters and loot is revealed.
help.doors.body:
{icon:door} A scenario is made of rooms. To open a door, step on its hex: a new room is revealed, and its monsters and loot appear at once.

After a room is opened, the turn can no longer be undone.

Some obstacles can be **broken**: attack them like an enemy (no modifier is drawn, the obstacle simply takes the attack value). Others can be **pushed aside**: standing next to one, spend movement on it.

A **barricade** or **rubble** in place of a door blocks the way until it is broken or pushed aside, then it opens the room behind. Only heroes break or move them.
help.loot.title: Loot: coins and chests
help.loot.short: Coins and chests are picked up at the end of the turn on your own hex.
help.loot.body:
{icon:coin} Coins and {icon:chest} chests lie on the board. A hero picks up everything on their hex at the end of their turn.

{icon:loot} **Loot N** on a card collects coins within N hexes.

After the scenario, coins turn into gold, and with gold you buy items in the camp.
help.attack.title: Attack
help.attack.short: Attack N: N damage plus the modifier, minus the target's Shield.
help.attack.body:
{icon:attack} **Attack N** hits an adjacent enemy (or a distant one if there is {icon:range} range).

How damage is counted:
1. The attack value on the card.
2. Plus bonuses from the card, items and orbs.
3. Plus a **modifier** from your deck.
4. Minus the target's {icon:shield} Shield ({icon:pierce} Pierce reduces it).

While you choose a target, the expected damage before the modifier is shown above the enemy.

If an attack has several {icon:targets} targets, each gets its own attack with its own modifier.
help.range.title: Ranged attack
help.range.short: Range N: a target up to N hexes away that you can see; an adjacent target gives disadvantage.
help.range.body:
{icon:ranged} A ranged attack has {icon:range} **range N**: you can hit a target up to N hexes away if you can see it.

**Line of sight** exists if at least one straight line between the corners of the two hexes does not cross a wall.

A ranged attack against an **adjacent** target has **disadvantage**: draw 2 modifiers and take the worse.
help.area.title: Area attack
help.area.short: The attack hits every enemy in the marked hexes.
help.area.body:
{icon:area} Some attacks have a shape: an arc in front of the hero, a line, a triangle. While choosing, turn and place the shape on the board; the attack hits every enemy in it.

Each target gets its own modifier.
help.modifiers.title: Attack modifiers
help.modifiers.short: Every attack draws a card from the deck: +0, ±1, ±2, ×2 or a miss.
help.modifiers.body:
Every attack draws one modifier card. Each hero has their own deck, the monsters share one.

The base deck of 20 cards: six +0, five +1, five −1, one +2 and one −2, one **×2** (doubles the damage) and one **miss** (the attack deals no damage).

When ×2 or a miss is drawn, the deck is reshuffled at the end of the round.

Perks change a hero's deck: they remove weak cards and add stronger ones.
help.advantage.title: Advantage and disadvantage
help.advantage.short: Advantage: draw 2 modifiers and take the better; disadvantage — the worse.
help.advantage.body:
**Advantage**: the attack draws 2 modifiers and takes the better. For example, the {icon:strengthen} Strengthen condition gives it.

**Disadvantage**: the attack draws 2 modifiers and takes the worse. {icon:muddle} Muddle gives it, and so does a ranged attack against an adjacent target.

If there are both advantage and disadvantage, they cancel each other out.
help.bless.title: Bless
help.bless.short: A ×2 card shuffled into the deck that disappears once drawn.
help.bless.body: {icon:bless} **Bless** is shuffled into the target's modifier deck. When it is drawn, the damage is doubled, and the card itself is removed from the deck.
help.curse.title: Curse
help.curse.short: A miss card shuffled into the deck that disappears once drawn.
help.curse.body: {icon:curse} **Curse** is shuffled into the target's modifier deck. When it is drawn, the attack misses, and the card itself is removed from the deck. Monsters can curse heroes; then the curse goes into the hero's deck.
help.shield.title: Shield
help.shield.short: Shield N reduces the damage of every attack by N.
help.shield.body:
{icon:shield} **Shield N** reduces the damage of every attack against the figure by N. A Shield from a card usually lasts until the end of the round.

Shield does not protect from damage without an attack: traps, Wound, hazardous terrain.

Several shields add up.
help.pierce.title: Pierce
help.pierce.short: Pierce N ignores N points of the target's Shield.
help.pierce.body: {icon:pierce} **Pierce N**: this attack ignores N points of the target's {icon:shield} Shield. Pierce 2 against Shield 3 leaves Shield 1.
help.retaliate.title: Retaliate
help.retaliate.short: Whoever attacks a figure with Retaliate N from an adjacent hex takes N damage.
help.retaliate.body:
{icon:retaliate} **Retaliate N**: every time an adjacent enemy attacks this figure, it takes N damage after its attack.

Retaliate does not answer ranged attacks from a distance.
help.push.title: Push and pull
help.push.short: Push N moves the target N hexes away from you, pull — towards you.
help.push.body:
{icon:push} **Push N**: after the attack the target is moved N hexes, each step farther from the one pushing.

{icon:pull} **Pull N**: the target is drawn N hexes closer.

You cannot push through walls, obstacles or other figures: the movement just stops earlier. You choose the path by tapping hexes.
help.heal.title: Heal
help.heal.short: Heal N restores N hit points (not above the maximum).
help.heal.body:
{icon:heal} **Heal N** restores N hit points, but not above the maximum.

Healing removes {icon:poison} Poison and {icon:wound} Wound. If the target is poisoned, the heal only removes the poison and restores no hit points.
help.provoke.title: Provoke
help.provoke.short: Nearby monsters attack the provoker if they can reach them.
help.provoke.body: {icon:provoke} **Provoke, radius N** (Warden): monsters within this radius target the Warden if they can attack him this turn. This way he takes the blows and protects his friends.
help.summon.title: Hero summons
help.summon.short: A hero's helper that acts on its own right before its owner.
help.summon.body: {icon:summon} Some heroes summon a helper (the Tinker — the clockwork dog Bolt). The helper acts on its own by the monster rules, but attacks enemies. It acts right before its hero.
help.followUp.title: Follow-up
help.followUp.short: An attack on an enemy another hero already hit this round: +1.
help.followUp.body:
{icon:targets} If you attack an enemy that **another** hero has already attacked this round, your attack gets +1.

After the first hit the game highlights such enemies: agree to hit one target together.
help.conditions.title: Conditions: overview
help.conditions.short: Eight conditions: harmful ones last until the end of the next turn or until healed.
help.conditions.body:
Conditions are shown as icons next to a figure. The icons differ by shape, not only by colour.

{icon:poison} Poison and {icon:wound} Wound last until the target is healed.

{icon:immobilize} Immobilize, {icon:disarm} Disarm, {icon:stun} Stun and {icon:muddle} Muddle last until the end of the target's next turn.

{icon:invisible} Invisible and {icon:strengthen} Strengthen are helpful conditions and last until the end of the next turn.
help.poison.title: Poison
help.poison.short: +1 damage from every attack on the target; healing only removes the poison.
help.poison.body:
{icon:poison} **Poison**: every attack on a poisoned figure deals +1 damage.

Lasts until the figure is healed. Healing a poisoned figure removes the poison but restores no hit points.
help.wound.title: Wound
help.wound.short: 1 damage at the start of every turn until healed.
help.wound.body:
{icon:wound} **Wound**: at the start of each of its turns the figure takes 1 damage. Shield does not protect from it.

Lasts until the figure is healed.
help.immobilize.title: Immobilize
help.immobilize.short: Cannot move until the end of its next turn.
help.immobilize.body:
{icon:immobilize} **Immobilize**: the figure cannot move (it can attack).

Lasts until the end of the target's next turn.
help.disarm.title: Disarm
help.disarm.short: Cannot attack until the end of its next turn.
help.disarm.body:
{icon:disarm} **Disarm**: the figure cannot attack (it can move).

Lasts until the end of the target's next turn.
help.stun.title: Stun
help.stun.short: Cannot act at all until the end of its next turn.
help.stun.body:
{icon:stun} **Stun**: the figure skips its actions: no movement, no attack, no healing. A stunned hero still picks cards, and they go to the discard.

Lasts until the end of the target's next turn.
help.muddle.title: Muddle
help.muddle.short: All the figure's attacks have disadvantage.
help.muddle.body:
{icon:muddle} **Muddle**: all of the figure's attacks have disadvantage (draw 2 modifiers, take the worse).

Lasts until the end of the target's next turn.
help.invisible.title: Invisible
help.invisible.body:
{icon:invisible} **Invisible**: enemies cannot attack this figure and move around as if it were not there.

Lasts until the end of the next turn.
help.strengthen.title: Strengthen
help.strengthen.short: All the figure's attacks have advantage.
help.strengthen.body:
{icon:strengthen} **Strengthen**: all of the figure's attacks have advantage (draw 2 modifiers, take the better).

Lasts until the end of the next turn.
help.orbs.title: Element orbs
help.orbs.short: Infuse — an orb appears above the hero; consume — take it from anywhere for a bonus.
help.orbs.body:
In the Fork there are three element orbs: {icon:orb-fire} **Fire** — more damage, {icon:orb-earth} **Earth** — protection and healing, {icon:orb-air} **Wind** — movement, range and pushing.

{icon:infuse} **Infuse X**: an orb of X appears above the hero. There can be only one orb of each element on the board; a new infusion renews it.

{icon:consume} **Consume X**: take the orb from anywhere on the board to get the bonus written on the card. Distance does not matter: you may take a friend's orb.

**Life of an orb**: at the end of the round it was made it dims, at the end of the next one it goes out.

Monsters neither make nor consume orbs. A card in your hand glows if its bonus will be available ("Attack 3 → 5").
help.elements.title: Elements (Base)
help.elements.short: Infuse makes an element strong; consuming a strong or waning one gives the card's bonus.
help.elements.body:
Under the Base rules there are six elements: {icon:fire} Fire, {icon:ice} Ice, {icon:air} Air, {icon:earth} Earth, {icon:light} Light, {icon:dark} Dark.

**Infuse** makes an element strong at the end of the turn. At the end of the round a strong element becomes waning, a waning one inert.

You can **consume** (spend) a strong or waning element for the bonus on a card. Monsters infuse and consume elements too.
help.momentum.title: Momentum and Surge
help.momentum.short: Cards with a lightning bolt give a charge; at 3 charges you may use your class Surge.
help.momentum.body:
{icon:momentum} Cards with a lightning mark add 1 **Momentum** charge when played. The bar is shown on the hero panel.

At 3 charges the hero may use their class **Surge** at any moment of their turn: the "Surge" button lights up. After that the bar resets. There are never more than 3 charges, so do not hold the Surge too long.

For example, the Warden's Surge gives Shield 2 to him and adjacent allies until the end of the round.
help.discard.title: Discard
help.discard.short: Played cards go to the discard; resting returns them to your hand.
help.discard.body:
{icon:discard} After a turn a normal card goes to the **discard**. Only resting brings it back.

Your hand shrinks every round: 2 cards per round. When few cards are left, it is time to rest.

{icon:hand} Hand, {icon:discard} discard and {icon:loss} lost cards are shown on the hero panel.
help.loss.title: Lost cards
help.loss.short: Cards with the loss mark are gone for the rest of the scenario after being played.
help.loss.body:
{icon:loss} A half with the loss mark is a strong action. After it the card goes to the **lost** pile: it will not come back until the end of the scenario, not even after resting.

Every rest also sends one card to the lost pile. When very few cards are left, the hero becomes exhausted, so save strong cards for important moments.
help.active.title: Active cards
help.active.short: Cards with a lasting effect stay in the active area while they work.
help.active.body: {icon:active} Some actions last longer than a turn: until the end of the round or for several uses (for example, Retaliate for 4 hits). Such a card stays in the **active area** on the hero panel until the effect ends, and then goes to the discard or the lost pile.
help.rest.title: Resting
help.rest.short: Short: at the end of the round, a random card is lost. Long: instead of a turn, heal 2 and choose the lost card.
help.rest.body:
Resting returns the discard to your hand, but one card is lost each time. You can rest when there are at least 2 cards in your discard.

{icon:rest} **Short rest** — at the end of the round, without spending a turn. The lost card is chosen **at random**. Once you may take 1 damage to lose another random card instead.

**Long rest** — declared instead of choosing cards, initiative 99. On their turn the hero **chooses** which card to lose, heals 2 and refreshes spent items.

A long rest is slower but safer: you decide what to lose.
help.avoidDamage.title: Avoid damage
help.avoidDamage.short: Cancel one source of damage: lose 1 card from your hand or 2 from the discard.
help.avoidDamage.body:
When a hero is about to be hurt, the game asks: take the damage or **avoid** it.

To avoid it, lose 1 card from your hand or 2 cards from your discard. The damage from this source is cancelled completely.

This is costly: it is usually better to take small damage and avoid only the damage that would exhaust the hero.
help.exhaustion.title: Exhaustion
help.exhaustion.short: A hero is exhausted at 0 hit points or when they can neither play 2 cards nor rest.
help.exhaustion.body:
A hero becomes **exhausted** when their hit points drop to 0, or when at the start of a round they can neither play 2 cards nor rest.

An exhausted hero leaves the board until the end of the scenario. If all heroes are exhausted, the scenario is lost.

In the Fork a hero at 0 hit points is first only **downed**: they can be raised.
help.revive.title: Raise an ally
help.revive.short: A downed ally next to you can be raised by spending a card half.
help.revive.body:
{icon:revive} In the Fork a hero at 0 hit points is **downed**: they lie on the board, do not act, and enemies do not target them.

An adjacent ally may spend the top or bottom action of a card to raise them with 3 hit points and the same hand.

Each hero can be raised once per scenario. The next fall is a normal exhaustion.
help.monsters.title: How monsters act
help.monsters.short: A monster goes to the nearest target it can attack and does what its card says.
help.monsters.body:
{icon:monster} The game controls the monsters by simple rules, without dice and without asking.

**Target.** A monster picks the hero it needs the least movement to attack. On a tie — the closer one in hexes, then the one who acts earlier this round.

**Movement.** A monster spends the least movement needed to attack its target. Ranged monsters do not step next to their target. They walk around traps if there is another way.

**Actions** are as on the behaviour card: move, attack, shield, heal. If the target is out of reach, the monster just comes closer.

Tap a monster on the board or on the initiative bar to see its hit points and plan.
help.elite.title: Elite monsters
help.elite.short: Stronger monsters with a golden frame; they act first in their group.
help.elite.body: {icon:elite} An **elite** monster has more hit points and a stronger attack, sometimes Shield or Retaliate too. It is recognised by its golden frame. In the group of its type the elite acts first.
help.intents.title: Three monster intents
help.intents.short: Before choosing cards you see 3 possible cards of a monster; one of them will be played.
help.intents.body:
{icon:approach} In the Fork, before cards are chosen, the game shows **three** possible behaviour cards for each monster type: initiative, action and an arrow to the likely target.

After the cards are chosen, one of the three is picked at random. So you know what to expect, but not exactly.

While you hold your finger on a card, the initiative bar shows where you will stand in the order among the monster intents.

The intents also warn about events: waves, calls for help, a runner raising the alarm.

Under these rules monsters have 10% more hit points.
help.items.title: Items
help.items.short: Items are buttons on the hero panel: they glow when they can be used.
help.items.body:
{icon:item} Items are on the hero panel. Each takes a slot: head, body, legs, hands or a small item.

**Spent** — turned over after use, comes back with a long rest. **Lost** — gone until the end of the scenario. **Passive** — always works.

An item glows when it can be used, and before an attack the game asks on its own: "Dagger: +1 Attack?". Some items work outside your turn: a shield when you are hit, a helmet before a monster attacks.
help.xp.title: Experience
help.xp.short: Marked parts of cards give experience if they are done.
help.xp.body:
{icon:xp} Parts of cards with the experience mark give XP when you actually do them (for example, the attack hit a target).

For winning a scenario each hero gets another 4 + 2 × scenario level experience.
help.levels.title: Levels and perks
help.levels.short: Experience raises the level: more hit points, a new card, a perk for the modifier deck.
help.levels.body:
Experience raises a hero's level: 20 XP — level 2, 45 — 3, 75 — 4, 110 — 5.

In a campaign the level goes up in the camp, on the "Level" tab. The game shows the new hit points, two new cards (you take one) and the perks, with the modifier deck now and after the perk next to them.

A **perk** improves the hero's modifier deck: removes −1 or −2, replaces weak cards with stronger ones or adds a +1 that infuses the class element.

A new card does not enlarge the hand: on the same tab you choose the cards for the mission. The scenario level depends on the heroes' levels and the difficulty.
help.initiativeDie.title: Initiative die
help.initiativeDie.short: A d12 is added to the number on the leading card: close cards sometimes swap places.
help.initiativeDie.body:
{icon:dice} Once the cards are revealed, every hero and every monster type rolls a d12 and adds it to the number on their card. The initiative bar shows the die tumbling, then "card + die = total", and the order lines up by the total.

The die gives 1 to 12. So cards 20 and 25 may swap places, but 15 and 60 never do. Want to be sure to go early? Take a card with a low number.

A long rest does not roll: its initiative is 99.

{icon:reroll} Dice items change the die. You can turn it off in Settings, under "Rules".
help.xCards.title: Cards with X
help.xCards.short: X on a card is a die with the faces 1 1 2 2 3 4, rolled when you act: "Attack 1+X" gives 2 to 5.
help.xCards.body:
{icon:dice} Some Rascal, Elementalist and Tinker cards have an X: "Attack 1+X", "Move 2+X", "Shield X". X is a special die with the faces 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, a little over 2 on average.

X is rolled when you play that action, not earlier. The game shows what came up. Then an attack modifier is drawn as usual: ×2 doubles the whole attack, and a miss is still a miss.

{icon:reroll} The X die can be rerolled with the Lucky Bone or the Luck Potion: the better of the two rolls counts.
help.monsterX.title: Monsters with X
help.monsterX.short: Some monsters strike with "Attack X": X is rolled as soon as the intent is revealed, so you see the exact number.
help.monsterX.body:
{icon:monster} Chaotic monsters such as the Mischief Gremlin and the Bandit Brute have cards with X. Their die is rolled right when the behaviour card is revealed, so the intent already shows the exact number, for example "Attack 3".

You know what is coming and have time to answer: step back, raise a shield or strike first.

Bosses have no X: their attacks are always predictable.
help.diceItems.title: Dice items
help.diceItems.short: The hourglass, potions, whistle, boots and bone reroll a die or shift your initiative.
help.diceItems.body:
{icon:reroll} These items are sold in the shop. Initiative items are used right after the roll, before the first turn: the game shows a window with the items you can use and a "Ready" button.

**Hourglass** — reroll your initiative die; the new roll stands.
**Agility Potion** — your die is 1 this round.
**Partner's Whistle** — swap your total initiative with an ally.
**Quiet Boots** — the leading card's initiative −10 or +10, but not below 1.
**Luck Potion** — reroll the initiative die or the X die and keep the better of the two.
**Lucky Bone** — for the X die: roll twice and keep the better.

Potions are lost, the rest are spent and come back with a long rest.
help.secondary.title: Secondary goals
help.secondary.short: Optional tasks of a scenario for extra experience or gold.
help.secondary.body:
{icon:objective-flag} Some scenarios have secondary goals: open a chest, get through with nobody exhausted, finish before a certain round or flip a lever.

They are optional: the scenario is won without them. But a secondary goal you meet gives the party a reward — experience or gold.

The goals are shown in the goal line at the top, next to the round number.
help.zones.title: Zones
help.zones.short: A marked area of the board: reach it, bring something there or keep monsters out of it.
help.zones.body:
{icon:compass} A zone is a few neighbouring hexes marked on the board. The scenario goal says what to do with it: reach the exit, bring an item there, lead a companion there, gather all heroes there or defend it against monsters.

If a goal has no zone, it simply names the hexes.
help.survive.title: Survive and defend
help.survive.short: Hold out for a set number of rounds; when defending, no monster may stand in the zone.
help.survive.body:
{icon:defend-point} **Survive.** You do not have to defeat everyone: last until the end of the given round and the scenario is won. Monsters come in waves, so you may hide and fall back.

**Defend.** The same, but at the end of every round no monster may stand in the defence zone. If one does, the scenario is lost.

The goal line at the top shows the round, for example "Defend: round 3/6".
help.escape.title: Escape
help.escape.short: Every hero on their feet must gather in the exit zone before the passage caves in.
help.escape.body:
{icon:door} In an escape you have to bring **all** heroes into the exit zone. A downed hero does not count: get them up first.

Time is short. If not everyone is there at the end of the given round, the passage caves in and the scenario is lost.

The goal line shows how many heroes are at the exit and how many rounds are left.
help.escort.title: Escort
help.escort.short: Lead a companion to the zone: they walk on their own while a hero is near and never fight.
help.escort.body:
{icon:escort} A companion is a scenario character you must lead to a zone. They have their own place on the initiative bar and walk to the goal on their own, but only while a hero is within 3 hexes of them.

The companion never attacks, but monsters can hit them. If they are downed, the scenario is lost. The goal line shows their hit points.

Stay close, cover them and clear the way.
help.collect.title: Collect
help.collect.short: Pick up the needed objects with a bottom action and carry them to the zone.
help.collect.body:
{icon:item} A "Collect" goal says what and how many, for example 3 crystals. Stand next to an object and play the bottom half of any card instead of its action: the hero picks the object up.

Objects are handed over at the end of the turn of a hero standing in the zone. The goal line counts how many are collected.

If a carrier is exhausted, everything they carried drops on their hex. Another hero can pick it up again.
help.levers.title: Levers and totems
help.levers.short: A lever is pulled with a card half and opens locked doors; a totem calls monsters while it stands.
help.levers.body:
{icon:lever} **Lever.** Stand next to it and play the card half the lever asks for instead of its action. The lever flips and opens doors that have no key.

**Objects with hit points.** Crates, totems and other things with a hit point number break under attacks, like enemies. A broken object leaves the board.

**Totem.** While a totem stands, it calls a monster next to itself at the start of every round. A "Destroy" goal asks you to break all such objects.
help.events.title: Scenario events
help.events.short: Ambushes, calls for help, alarms and waves bring new monsters; the intents warn you in advance.
help.events.body:
{icon:monster} A scenario can change in the middle of a fight.

**Ambush.** When you open a door or step on a certain spot, monsters appear, and your move stops on that hex.

**Call for help.** A horn-blower calls for help if it survives a few of its turns. Defeat it sooner and nobody comes.

**Alarm.** A monster runs to a door or a bell and attacks nobody. Catch it before it gets there: instead of a new wave there is a reward.

**Waves.** On certain rounds new enemies arrive.

{icon:approach} The monster intents and the round forecast warn you: "Next round arrive…", "will call for help in round 3". A counter shows over the horn-blower and the runner.
help.campaign.title: Campaign map
help.campaign.short: The next mission is chosen on the map of the land; some forks open one path and close another.
help.campaign.body:
{icon:map} A campaign is a series of missions with the same heroes. Experience, gold and items carry over between missions, and progress saves itself. Start it from the main menu with "Campaign".

The next mission is chosen on the map of the land. The markers show: won, ready to go (pulsing), path closed, unknown place. A won mission can be replayed and a lost one tried again.

**Forks.** Sometimes you choose one of two paths, for example the short way through the mine or the long way over the pass. The chosen path opens and the other turns grey. The choice decides who becomes a friend, what appears in the shop and which missions come next.
help.story.title: Story
help.story.short: Talks before a mission, lines in battle and after it; in Settings: full, short or off.
help.story.body:
{icon:light} The Guild of the Brave lives at the Plump Goose inn in the town of Alba. The Gloom befuddles animals and spirits, and the heroes gather the broken Guardian Lantern and drive the fog away. Nobody dies here: defeated enemies simply run off.

Before a mission there is a short talk, in battle lines appear in speech bubbles and in a banner at the top, after the mission there is an ending, and in the camp a word from Mrs Marta.

In Settings, the "Story" row: **Full**, **Short** (only the main lines) or **Off**. A campaign keeps this choice with it.
help.camp.title: Camp
help.camp.short: Between missions the party is in the camp: equipment, shop, new levels and the next mission.
help.camp.body:
{icon:rest} After a campaign mission the "To the camp" button brings the party to the inn. On the left are the heroes, each with their own colour and their own gold.

**Equipment** — the hero's slots, their chest and the party chest.
**Shop** — buy, sell, upgrade, gift gold.
**Level** — a new level once there is enough experience, and the cards for the mission.

The "To the mission" button shows a summary, and the party sets out.
help.shop.title: Shop
help.shop.short: Each hero buys with their own gold; selling gives half the price.
help.shop.body:
{icon:gold} Each hero has their own gold: it comes from coins on the board and mission rewards.

The shop shows item cards with the effect, slot and price. The filter at the top shows items for one slot. New wares appear as the party completes story missions.

**Buy** — the item goes to the current hero. **Sell** — for half the price, rounded down.

Slots: head, body, legs, hands (two one-handed things or one two-handed) and small items — as many as half the hero's level, rounded up.
help.upgrade.title: Item upgrades
help.upgrade.short: Every item can be upgraded once for its own price; an upgraded item has a plus in its name.
help.upgrade.body:
{icon:up} The **Upgrade** button in the shop makes an item a little stronger. It costs as much as the item itself, and an item can be upgraded only once.

An upgraded item has a plus in its name and a golden glow in its slot. For example, "Dagger+" gives +2 to a melee attack, "Healing Potion+" heals 4, "Chainmail+" gives Shield 2.

It sells for half the sum of the price and the upgrade.
help.gifts.title: Gifts
help.gifts.short: A hero is short of gold? Another hero can gift them 5 gold.
help.gifts.body:
{icon:coin} Each hero's gold is separate, so you can see who earned what. But you can share: the shop has a "Gift 5 gold" button for every other hero.

Agree who needs it more right now: a new shield for the Warden is often more useful than a third potion.
help.partyChest.title: Party chest
help.partyChest.short: Found items and mission rewards go into a shared chest; any hero can take them.
help.partyChest.body:
{icon:chest} Items found in battle and mission rewards go into the **party chest** on the "Equipment" tab. Tap an item to give it to the current hero.

Each hero also has their own chest: their things that are not worn right now. Tap an item to put it on.

An item from the party chest can also be sold or upgraded in the shop.
help.drops.title: Loot from chests and enemies
help.drops.short: Chests and defeated enemies give coins or an item; in a campaign items go to the party chest.
help.drops.body:
{icon:loot} A chest on the board may hold coins, an item or both. It is opened by the hero who ends their turn on its hex.

A defeated monster sometimes leaves coins on its hex, and strong enemies and bosses an item. Coins are picked up as usual, and an item is added to the finds at once.

The end screen shows everything found, and in a campaign it goes to the party chest.
help.diagram.card.name: Card name
help.diagram.ini.order: order of turns in the round
help.diagram.piles.rest: resting returns the discard to the hand
tutorial.offer.title: First game?
tutorial.offer.text: The tutorial is a short scenario with a helper: it shows how to choose cards, move and attack, and what orbs, momentum and resting are. It takes about 10–15 minutes.
tutorial.coach.name: Helper
tutorial.coach.skipSure: End it now? You can play the tutorial again from the menu.
tutorial.done.title: Tutorial complete!
tutorial.done.text: Now you know the basics. The rest of the rules is always in the rules reference, and hints for each hero are switched on in the settings. In a campaign the camp waits between missions: the shop, new levels and the map of the land.
tutorial.lost.title: Not this time
tutorial.lost.text: No worries: this is how you learn. Try again or go on to a real game.
scenario.s0: Tutorial: the yard of the Plump Goose
scenario.s0.intro: Mistress Marta looks out of the kitchen: "The rats are climbing out of the cellar again! Warden, chase them away, and meanwhile I will show you how things work around here."
scenario.s0.outro: The yard is clean, and Mistress Marta wipes her hands on her apron with a smile: "Now you are real Bravehearts."
tutorial.step.welcome.title: Welcome to the Braveheart Guild!
tutorial.step.welcome.text: I am the helper and will guide you through the first fight. You play the Warden: he is sturdy, carries a shield and protects his friends. I will light up where to tap and explain why. Press "Next".
tutorial.step.intro.title: Scenario goal
tutorial.step.intro.text: This says what to do: defeat all the rats. The goal is also shown later in the game menu. Press "{button}".
tutorial.step.curtain.title: Pass the tablet
tutorial.step.curtain.text: Before choosing cards the game hides the hand so that nobody peeks. With several players, pass the tablet to the one named on the screen. Tap the screen.
tutorial.step.hand.title: Your hand
tutorial.step.hand.text: These are your cards. Each round you pick two. Tap "Shield Bash" (it opens large) and press "Pick", then do the same with "Earth Strike". The first card you pick leads.
tutorial.step.leading.title: The leading card
tutorial.step.leading.text: One of the two cards is leading {icon:initiative}: its number (initiative) decides when you act. Lower means earlier. "Shield Bash" (15) is already leading, so the Warden acts before the rats. You can make the other card leading with the "{button}" button.
tutorial.step.ready.title: Ready!
tutorial.step.ready.text: Two cards picked, the leading one marked. Press "{button}": the cards are revealed, and the turns begin.
tutorial.step.order.title: Order of turns
tutorial.step.order.text: At the top is the initiative bar: who acts after whom this round. Your Warden goes before the rats.
tutorial.step.die.title: Initiative die
tutorial.step.die.text: {icon:dice} Everyone adds a d12 to the number on their card: the Warden to 15, the rats to their own number. That is why the order is a little different every time. Want to be sure to go early? Take a card with a low number.
tutorial.step.plan.title: A monster's plan
tutorial.step.plan.text: Tap a rat on the bar or on the board: you will see its hit points, attack and what it will do this round. Monsters always go for the nearest target.
tutorial.step.halfMove.title: Move first
tutorial.step.halfMove.text: Your turn! Play the bottom half of "Shield Bash": Move 3. Tap it.
tutorial.step.hex.title: Where to go
tutorial.step.hex.text: The lit hexes are where you can go. Tap the marked hex next to a rat, then tap again or "{button}".
tutorial.step.halfAttack.title: Now attack
tutorial.step.halfAttack.text: Now the top of "Earth Strike": Attack 3 and an Earth orb. Tap the top half.
tutorial.step.target.title: Choose a target
tutorial.step.target.text: Tap the rat next to you. Above it you see how much damage it will take before the modifier. Confirm with a second tap or "{button}".
tutorial.step.infuse.title: Infuse Earth
tutorial.step.infuse.text: The second part of this action is to infuse Earth. Some steps of a card need no target: press "{button}".
tutorial.step.modifier.title: Attack modifier
tutorial.step.modifier.text: Every attack draws a card from your modifier deck: +1, −1, ×2 or even a miss. This time it was {mod}, so the damage is {damage}.
tutorial.step.orb.title: Earth orb
tutorial.step.orb.text: "Earth Strike" infused Earth: an orb appeared above the Warden. You can consume it next round for a bonus (for the Warden — Shield). Orbs do not last long: it dims at the end of this round and goes out at the end of the next.
tutorial.step.momentum.title: Momentum
tutorial.step.momentum.text: Cards with a lightning bolt add a momentum charge: the bar on the hero panel. At three charges you can use the Warden's Surge: Shield 2 for him and friends next to him.
tutorial.step.endTurn.title: End your turn
tutorial.step.endTurn.text: Both halves are played. Press "{button}": the cards go to the discard, and the next one acts.
tutorial.step.monsters.title: The monsters' turn
tutorial.step.monsters.text: Now the rats act. The game controls the monsters: they come closer and attack by their card. Watch.
tutorial.step.avoid.title: You are bitten!
tutorial.step.avoid.text: A rat attacks. You can take the damage or avoid it by losing cards. 1–2 damage is a trifle, so choose "{button}". Keep your cards.
tutorial.step.shortRest.title: Short rest
tutorial.step.shortRest.text: End of the round. A short rest returns the discard to your hand, but one random card is lost. You still have many cards in hand, so "{button}" is better now.
tutorial.step.round2.title: A new round
tutorial.step.round2.text: Now pick the cards yourself. Look for ones that fit: walk up to a rat and strike. A card with a glowing bonus can consume the Earth orb.
tutorial.step.consume.title: Consume the orb
tutorial.step.consume.text: See the glowing line? The Earth orb pays for this bonus: play this half, and the orb is consumed. You may also take someone else's orb; distance does not matter.
tutorial.step.surge.title: Surge!
tutorial.step.surge.text: Three momentum charges! The "{button}" button glows: press it at any time during your turn. The bar resets afterwards.
tutorial.step.openDoor.title: Open the door
tutorial.step.openDoor.text: There are no more rats in the yard, but that is not all. Step on the door (the marked hex): the cellar opens, with new enemies inside.
tutorial.step.door.title: A new room
tutorial.step.door.text: You opened a door: a new room is revealed, with monsters and loot. The turn that opened the door can no longer be undone.
tutorial.step.loot.title: Loot
tutorial.step.loot.text: Coins and chests are picked up at the end of the turn on the hex where the hero stands. After the scenario the coins become gold.
tutorial.step.longRest.title: Time to rest
tutorial.step.longRest.text: Few cards are left in your hand. Instead of cards press "{button}". You will act last (initiative 99), but you choose which card to lose, heal 2 and get the discard back into your hand.
tutorial.step.longRestLoss.title: Which card to lose?
tutorial.step.longRestLoss.text: Choose the card you can most easily do without. The rest of the discard returns to your hand.
tutorial.step.free.title: On your own now
tutorial.step.free.text: You know the basics! Finish the fight: the door leads to the cellar, with one more rat and a chest. I will tell you when something new comes up.
tutorial.step.wait.title: Wait
